title: Stating the exact coin flip posterior
summary: The coin flip example README now names the closed-form posterior, Beta(24, 18). This gives readers an exact target to compare against MCMC output. A source check of data.csv and both model files supports the stated value.

blocks.text:
MCMC.js is a command-line tool that runs Bayesian models in Turing.jl, JuliaBUGS or Stan, checks whether the sampler converged, and shows the results. The examples directory has small models that new users run with `mcmc run`.

This draft PR adds one line to the coin flip example README. The line names the exact posterior distribution for the example data. Only documentation changes. No code, data or model files change, so CLI users and library consumers are not affected.

blocks.title: examples/coin_flip/README.md after the run command
blocks.before: The data has 23 heads in 40 tosses, so `p` concentrates near 0.575.
blocks.after:
The data has 23 heads in 40 tosses, so `p` concentrates near 0.575.
The posterior is `Beta(24, 18)` with the `Beta(1, 1)` prior.

blocks.text: The Beta prior is conjugate to the Bernoulli likelihood. With prior Beta(a, b), h heads and t tails, the posterior is Beta(a + h, b + t). Both model files use a Beta(1, 1) prior on `p` and an independent Bernoulli(p) likelihood for each toss, so the closed form applies to the Julia and Stan versions alike. With the new line, readers can compare the sampled mean and intervals with an exact answer instead of only the approximate 0.575.

blocks.title: Posterior parameters match the data and models
blocks.text: This is a source check, not a test run. The 40 rows of `y` in data.csv were counted by hand: 23 are 1 and 17 are 0. Both models use p ~ Beta(1, 1) and Bernoulli(p) per observation. The conjugate update gives Beta(1 + 23, 1 + 17) = Beta(24, 18), which matches the new line.

blocks.title: 0.575 is the posterior mode, not its mean
blocks.text: Beta(24, 18) has mode 23/40 = 0.575 and mean 24/42 ≈ 0.571. The existing sentence says `p` concentrates near 0.575, which is correct for the mode. A reader comparing it with the `mean` column of `mcmc run` will see about 0.571. Stating the mean next to the new line would prevent that small mismatch. This is an optional wording suggestion. The text is not wrong as written.

blocks.title: Optional wording for the new line
blocks.text: This is a suggested edit, not part of the PR. It shows where the posterior parameters come from, gives the mean that `mcmc run` reports, and avoids repeating the prior already named on line 4.
blocks.before: The posterior is `Beta(24, 18)` with the `Beta(1, 1)` prior.
blocks.after: The exact posterior is `Beta(1 + 23, 1 + 17) = Beta(24, 18)`, with mean 24/42 ≈ 0.571 and mode 0.575.
